labctl.notes: HOST-NATIVE since the 2026-09 de-bridging (docs/lab/IRIS-DEBRIDGE-LEDGER.md): the museum's fork of Iris runs on the host inside a systemd-nspawn container -- no captured Debian, no QEMU, no QMP, no X server, no window. Frames IFB1 shm, input mamectl/1, audio off. `labctl exec` has no ssh channel here: the bridge era's port 5839 reached the Debian kiosk, not the emulated Indy, and the kiosk is gone. The machine's own exec is Iris's ci socket at /data/vms/streamhost/stations/indyr4400/run/iris-ci.sock (serial-send / wait-serial / serial-read). It carries ONLY the exec channel: the reset verbs ride the station's one mamectl/1 socket at run/ctl.sock, with the pointer and the keys. Iris's monitor console listens on IRIS_MONITOR_ADDR (127.0.0.1:18136 here; upstream hardcodes 8888) inside the container's private netns: reach it with `nsenter -t $(cat /data/vms/streamhost/stations/indyr4400/mame.pid) -n`, never from the host directly. Pointer is ABSOLUTE through a closed loop against Iris's VC2 hardware-cursor registers -- the mechanism the MAME `irix` sibling already runs against this same IRIX 6.5 X server. See docs/guests/indyr4400.md.

# indyr4400 — Iris -> SGI Indy (MIPS R4400) -> IRIX 6.5.22, HOST-NATIVE.
#   The SECOND SGI Indy in the lineup and the other emulator: 'irix' is MAME's
#   R4600 indy_4610 running BARE-METAL (MAME panics under a KVM vCPU); this one
#   is userspace Rust, de-bridged in 2026-09 and now running on the host inside a
#   systemd-nspawn container with no QEMU, no kiosk and no X. The 6.3 GB IRIX disk
#   is a READ-ONLY asset staged by stations/indyr4400/fetch-assets.sh.

museum.blurb: The other Indy. SGI sold the 1993 pizza-box in several MIPS grades, and this is the R4400 — the faster, larger-cache sibling of the R4600 next to it in the hall, and the chip SGI put in the Indigo² and the Challenge servers. Same blue case, same 24-bit XL graphics, same IRIX 6.5 — a different processor inside, and the reason the two sit side by side.
museum.notes: Live streamhost station, HOST-NATIVE since the 2026-09 de-bridging (rule 13). Iris (github.com/techomancer/iris, BSD-3; the museum runs a fork), a userspace Rust SGI Indy emulator, runs directly on the host inside a systemd-nspawn container and publishes its own framebuffer and input planes -- there is no captured Debian kiosk, no QEMU, no X server and no window left in the path. It was a bridge until then, and the conversion is why: one pointer move took 361 ms to reach the framebuffer through QEMU PS/2 -> guest X -> winit -> llvmpipe -> dbus, against 68 ms for the host-native MAME `irix` sibling. The DELIBERATE pair to that station: same museum machine, different silicon (R4400 vs R4600) and a different emulator. Pointer is absolute through a closed loop on Iris's VC2 hardware-cursor registers; audio and networking are still off. archetype beige-tower-crt. See docs/guests/indyr4400.md.

reset.fixture: SGI Indy (MIPS R4400, 256 MB, XL 24-bit) IRIX 6.5.22 on the Indigo Magic Desktop (4Dwm, demos session) in the museum's fork of Iris, HOST-NATIVE at 1280x1024: no kiosk, no QEMU, no X server, no window. Reset is an in-process restore of the IRIS_STATE snapshot over the station's one mamectl/1 socket (LOADST golden, measured 0.19-1.6 s), with a ~7-minute cold boot as the loud bounded fallback after two launches that restore and never ack. Converted from the QEMU bridge on 2026-09-10; the bridge's loadvm-golden checkpoint is retired with the kiosk that held it. mouse/keyboard UNVERIFIED until the real-browser probe clears them.
